To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the L2108–120 epitope fused to the N-terminus of PVX CP was efficiently expressed in plants, that the epitope was immunogenic after vaccination of mice, and that the epitope could be expressed in plants as a C-terminal fusion to the PVX CP.

the HPV-16 L2108- 120 epitope can be expressed in plants as a fusion protein with PVX CP and can induce an immune response against the L2 epitope after immunization of animals with this vaccine candidate.

the HPV-16 L2108-20 epitope fused to the PVX coat-protein was successfully expressed in transgenic plants, and the immunization of mice with the fusion protein resulted in the production of antibodies against both epitopes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach for the production of immunogenic virus-like particles based on PVX CP and HPV-16 L2108- 120 fusion protein.
the production and evaluation of a plant-based HPV vaccine.
the development of a plant-made vaccine based on a viral vector and the HPV-16 L2108- 120 epitope.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PVX-based vector system is a promising candidate for the development of vaccines for the treatment of human papillomavirus-associated diseases.
the L2108-PVX CP fusion protein was successfully expressed in transgenic N. benthamiana plants and the fusion protein was able to induce an immune response in mice.
this fusion protein can be used to produce a vaccine against human papillomavirus infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient and cost-effective system for the production and immunization with a plant-derived HPV-16 L2108- 120 epitope fused to PVX CP.
the L2-derived epitope was successfully expressed in transgenic plants and that the L2 epitope-PVX CP fusion protein was recognized by antibodies in mice sera.
the L2108–120 epitope fused to the PVX CP is expressed in plants and the fusion protein can be used as a vaccine candidate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PVX-based vectors are promising tools for transient expression of foreign epitopes in plants.
PVX-based vectors are suitable tools for the production of plant-derived vaccines.

the epitope derived of HPV-16 L2108-20 can be expressed as fusion with the coat protein of PVX in transgenic plants and the resulting fusion protein is able to induce the production of antibodies in animals after immunization.
